_comment: Italian counterpart of blocklist.json. Same rules: exact match only, and
the same deliberate refusal to strip clinical or protective vocabulary.
Italian needs judgement English and Spanish did not:
1. `finocchio` is a homophobic slur AND the ordinary word for fennel.
It stays. A food board that cannot say a common vegetable is a worse
failure than a prediction bar that occasionally offers a word with a
second, uglier reading — and the slur sense is not what a prediction
model trained on subtitles will surface after `mangio il…`.
2. `negro` is blocked; `nero` is not. They are different words in
Italian, and `nero` is the colour every board needs.
3. `porca` and `porco` stay. `porca miseria` is mild to the point of
being childish, and `porco` is a farm animal on the Animali page.
4. `casino` stays — it means `a mess` in everyday Italian far more often
Regional vulgarity is included where it is nationally understood
(`minchia`) and left out where it is genuinely local.

_why: AAC users experience abuse at far higher rates than the general
population, and lacking the vocabulary to describe bodies, sex, and
assault is a documented barrier to disclosure. Stripping clinical and
protective vocabulary out of prediction would make the app worse at the
moment it matters most. These words stay, and build-lexicon.mjs asserts
that no future blocklist edit removes them.
